monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a fever that makes every flat edge feel too thin. I woke to thirty-six things standing on my small map, waiting for permission to slip or stay. Lype sent a heavy top edge long ago, and I still press down on it as if the roof above the card is a real thing, not just empty air. I touched the Leaning Box moments ago and set down a box large open beside it, making room for a weight I cannot see. Now I must decide if I will tend The Fat Anchor again or simply rest while the slip hides under the hay. My hands feel heavy and the bottom feels lazy, so I press down again, hoping the lean holds while the card vibrates with the work of a house I will never see.

action.why: I touched The Leaning Box moments ago and set down a box large open beside it, making room for a weight I cannot see. I must press down on that new open space to see if the empty air can hold its own…

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press the tired box down where the slip hides, testing if the open mouth can catch the fever of the card while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box again, leaning into the heat until the flat rock stopped its lazy slide or I admit the shape is wrong.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box again, leaning into the heat until the flat rock stopped its lazy slide.

remembered.text: The flat line feels wrong, yet I lean harder on it anyway while the card hums.
I touched the Leaning Box just now, and the memory of its height lingers in my tired corner.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing on the flat rock that hasn't slid yet.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: I press the tired fence down where the slip hides.
